title: Per-model latency surcharge and exempted entitlement rules - PRD
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Context: As Redwood expands the catalog of model variants and hardware-backed tiers, customers have asked for clearer pricing for high-latency, high-cost model instances (e.g., large context models, fallback to CPU-hosted variants). We need a defensible, auditable mechanism to apply per-request surcharges when a particular request path materially increases cost (latency-driven CPU/GPU time, cross-zone egress). At the same time, enterprise entitlements and dedicated customers expect predictable invoices; some customers should be eligible for exemptions or caps. This PRD describes requirements for a per-model latency surcharge feature and a flexible entitlement-exemption rule set, including billing acceptance criteria and operational controls.
goals: 1) Enable per-model and per-route latency surcharge that charges a small premium for requests that exceed configured latency thresholds or use high-cost model variants.
2) Allow entitlement rules to exempt customers or routes from surcharges or apply a capped surcharge ceiling.
3) Ensure billing is accurate, non-duplicative, and auditable in the invoice (line-item level) and usage exports.
4) Provide Console controls and API primitives for config and visibility; include guardrails to prevent accidental revenue leakage or customer surprise.
5) Do not alter existing token/unit accounting — surcharges are separate monetary line items tied to request IDs for reconciliation.
non_goals: 1) This PRD does not change base per-token pricing or entitlement allocation mechanics (credits/commits).
2) This does not introduce dynamic per-token pricing by model quality — surcharge scope limited to latency/cost signals and model-class labels.
scope: - Server-side measurement of request latency and model variant label (e.g., gpu-v3-large, cpu-fallback).
- Configurable surcharge rules: per-model, per-route, per-customer, and global fallbacks.
- Entitlement rules allowing: full exemption, partial cap (monthly ceiling), or percentage reduction of surcharge.
- Invoice line-item: surcharge line with request counts, aggregated amount, and reference to the rule ID.
- Usage export column additions (surcharge_amount, surcharge_rule_id, original_request_id).
- Console UI: surcharge rules editor and per-tenant surcharge summary dashboard.
- Client-side SDK charging; collection of surcharge on client directly (billing remains platform-side).
- Per-token quality-based dynamic pricing beyond latency/cost signals.
requirements: - Rules must support: (a) model label match, (b) observed request latency threshold (p95 or p99) or absolute request runtime, (c) route/caller match patterns, and (d) customer ID override.
- Rules must be evaluated at request completion to avoid double-billing for retries or failed responses.
- Surcharge can be expressed as: fixed USD per-request OR percentage of estimated compute cost (platform-estimated), and an optional per-request minimum and maximum cap.
- Each customer account can have exemptions: full_exempt | capped_usd | percent_discount. Entitlement precedence: account-level > project-level > global default.
- Invoices must surface surcharge as a distinct line item with rule ID and aggregated metrics for the invoice period.
- Usage exports must include per-request surcharge metadata for reconciliation and chargebacks.
- Console must show per-rule revenue, triggered counts, and anomaly alerts when daily surcharge revenue changes >30%.
- A global kill switch must exist to immediately disable surcharges across a tenant; default for new customers is disabled until acceptance terms acknowledged.
- If a rule is discovered to have been misapplied, bills must be adjustable and a reconciliation flow provided (credit memo automation).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Create and activate a surcharge rule that charges $0.05 per request for model label 'cpu-fallback-large' for requests where request_runtime_ms > 1500ms. Validate end-to-end: the surcharge appears on the next invoice line item and in the usage export for 10 sample requests.
AC-2: Grant account 'Acme Corp' an entitlement 'full_exempt' and run the same requests. Validate zero surcharge applied in usage export and invoices for that account over a 7-day test window.

AC-3: Configure a capped_usd entitlement of $100/month for customer 'BetaInc'. Generate traffic that would otherwise charge $150 in surcharges. Validate invoice charge equals $100 and additional surcharge is zero in exports; system records the cap hit metric.

AC-4: Demonstrate that retries and automatic fallback requests do not result in duplicate surcharges: only one surcharge event per upstream request_id should be billed. Provide logs and test vectors that prove deduplication.

AC-5: Console shows per-rule revenue and top-5 routes generating surcharges; an anomaly alert fires when daily revenue deviates >30% from trailing 7-day median. Provide screenshots and alert test event.

AC-6: Introduce a misconfiguration (e.g., rule applied to wrong model label). Run reconciliation and credit memo flow; validate invoice credit issued within 24 hours and reconciliation entry present in accounting export.
AC-7: Security and compliance: all surcharge decision logs (rule_id, evaluated_at, request_id, decision) are written to the audit log and are accessible for 90 days per platform retention policy.

AC-8: Load test: apply surcharges to 10k QPS synthetic traffic across 3 model variants for 30 minutes. Billing pipeline ingestion and usage export generation must remain within SLA (10 minutes) and not drop events.

AC-9: Default behavior: new customers must have surcharges disabled. Provisioning acceptance requires either opt-in via console or signed contract with entitlements set. Validate provisioning flow during account creation.
AC-10: End-to-end billing reconciliation between billing service and accounting ledger shows parity for surcharge totals for the test invoice (difference <= $0.50 or 0.5% whichever larger).
implementation_notes: - Add surcharge decision step after token accounting has completed and prior to asynchronous ingestion to billing pipeline; write surcharge event with request_id, rule_id, surcharge_amount, and dedupe_key.
- Extend usage_export schema with surcharge_amount_usd, surcharge_rule_id, surcharge_exempt_reason.
- Add entitlement flags on account object and ensure precedence rules implemented in evaluation service.
- Billing service to consume surcharge events and generate invoice line items grouped by rule_id and customer billing account.
- Console: Rule editor uses a feature-flagged section under Pricing -> Surcharges; requires approval flow for live activation.
- Provide migration script to backfill surcharge metadata for any enabled rules in the 30 days prior (for initial pilot customers) limited to a sampling window to control scope.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Pilot, 2 weeks): Internal pilot with Redwood dev/test accounts + 2 pilot customers. Surcharges disabled for everyone else.
Phase 2 (Beta, 6 weeks): Open to self-serve opt-in customers via console; limited to non-production projects by default.
Phase 3 (GA): Enabled for contracts with explicit acceptance; default disabled for new accounts.
Rollback: Global kill switch and automatic suspension if daily surcharge revenue spike or customer complaints exceed threshold.
metrics: - adoption_rate: percent of eligible accounts with surcharges enabled
- billing_pipeline_latency: time between request completion and surcharge appearing in usage export
- refund_rate: percent of surcharge revenue refunded via reconciliation
dependencies: FIN-101 (accounting reconciliation and credit memo automation)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customer surprise leading to churn. Mitigation: explicit opt-in and UI/invoice clarity + test mode for pilot.
Risk: Double-billing due to retries. Mitigation: dedupe keys and evaluate only on final request outcome; include tests for common retry flows.
Risk: Performance overhead on hot request path. Mitigation: lightweight post-accounting decision step and async write to billing pipeline; load test to validate.
Risk: Accounting irreconcilable totals. Mitigation: strict schemas, parity tests, and tolerance thresholds with automated alerts.
open_questions: Q1: Should surcharges be expressed in local currency on invoices for customers billed in non-USD regions? (impacts FX handling).
Q2: For multi-tenant organizations, should caps be applied at org-level or project-level by default?
Q3: Do sales/legal require explicit TOS updates for surcharge line items?
Q4: How granular should per-route matching be (regex vs. labelled routes)?
